summary.title: Linux disk I/O diagram
summary.one_liner: A layered diagram of the Linux disk I/O stack, from application calls through VFS, the filesystem, block and scheduler layers, and drivers down to HDD, SSD and NVMe hardware.
keywords: how does linux handle disk reads and writes
takeaways: The Linux disk I/O path has distinct layers: application, VFS (direct I/O or buffer/page cache), filesystem, optional block layer, generic block layer, disk scheduler, block device driver, and hardware.
The disk scheduler layer can use either blk-mq or the classic I/O schedulers such as noop, anticipatory, deadline and cfq.
Hardware at the bottom may be a RAID or disk controller with HDD, SSD or NVMe drives.
The diagram is part of the Croatian-language book 'Operativni sustavi i računalne mreže - Linux u primjeni' and is provided as a downloadable PDF poster.
summary.summary: This Zenodo record (version 3, published April 17, 2024) provides a poster-style diagram of the Linux disk I/O subsystem and the commands used at each layer. The description lists the layers in order: application, VFS (direct I/O or buffer and page cache), filesystem, optional and generic block layers, disk scheduler (blk-mq or classic schedulers), block device driver, and hardware such as RAID or disk controllers with HDD, SSD or NVMe drives. The diagram is linked to the DOI of an accompanying book and is available as an English PDF. The page text gives only the layer outline and no in-depth explanation.
